Strict-H1 mixed net-female-fitness effect. Single host-specific pollinators were experimentally introduced at 0,4,8,12,16,20,24 and >=28 days after syconium receptivity began. Because the same monoecious syconia produce both seeds and pollinator galls, final seed count already reflects pollination benefit after ovule allocation/larval cost. Table-1 seed means±SD and n were transformed as log(mean seeds); delta-method variances s^2/(n*m^2) supplied inverse-variance weights. Weighted log-linear slope across all eight source groups = -0.03334257 log seed count per additional day waited; SE=0.00306271, variance=9.3802e-06. The >=28 group model age is 28.94545 days, the source-sample-weighted mean of 46 day-28, 5 day-32 and 4 day-36 syconia. Positive oriented effect means closer synchrony -> greater final seed output.

First quantitatively closed strict-H1 antagonist programme. Frozen primary subset uses temp=control and snow=normal. For each focal plant, flowering availability (open+buds) is compared with a leave-one-out Hylemya oviposition activity curve from all other primary plants; both curves are normalized over valid census dates and overlap is histogram intersection. Final fitness is the source-coded seeds_per_flower reconstructed from raw fruit/seed records with source R NA propagation preserved. Pinned external source jmpowers/ipomopsis-temp@9f4ceff87f5eb68c5a09f5e89ea457432e452542 reconstructs n=11, Pearson r=-0.05224909311004083, Fisher z=-0.05229671725455789, variance=1/(11-3)=0.125. Native synchrony direction is retained: the estimate is essentially null, with a slight negative association between greater antagonist overlap and seed production per flower.

Strict-H1 categorical overlap effect. The source sampled 90 different plants during the population flowering peak when legitimate oil-bee visitation was scarce and 90 different plants 3-4 weeks later when pollinator activity was high, explicitly treating these as strongly contrasting flowering-pollinator overlap states. The seed-set GLM (n=173 after tag loss) used natural vs hand pollination and flowering time; under the source coding, the flowering-time coefficient +1.55±0.25 is the late/high-overlap vs peak/low-overlap log-odds contrast for the natural-pollination reference condition. Variance=0.25^2. Pollinator visitation evidence is independent of seed outcome: legitimate-visit lesions occurred on 7.5% of 134 peak flowers vs 93.6% of 140 late flowers. Positive native direction therefore already means greater synchrony -> higher natural seed set. No conversion to Fisher-z is made.

Strict-H1 source-ordered low-versus-high pollinator-availability contrast. S. graminifolia clones were divided into independent early (peak before 1 Sep 1980; n=10) and late (n=27) groups. Apis was first recorded on 28 Aug and uncommon before 1 Sep, then became the dominant September visitor. Natural filled-seed means and 95% CIs from Table 5/10 were inverted on the source angular scale (asin(sqrt(p))); group SDs were recovered from transformed 95% CIs using Student-t critical values. Hedges g for higher vs lower Apis availability = +1.140160763709139; sampling variance = 0.14974957430600422. S. canadensis, S. nemoralis and S. juncea are excluded from this primary row under the frozen species-identification rule in docs/EXTRACTION_IWE084.md. This source-native SMD is not silently converted to Fisher-z.
